$$
{(x,y)\in {{field-1}}\,:\,y\,{{field-2}}\,2x-3}
$$
after.worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *below* the line $y=2x-3.$

Therefore, a point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following condition is satisfied:

$$
y<2x-3
$$

We must also include the line $y=2x-3$ since the boundary is included in the set (the curve is solid). So, we change the inequality symbol above as follows:

$$
y\le 2x-3
$$

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,y\le 2x-3}.
$$

content.worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *above* the line $y=-2$ and *below* the line $y=x.$

A point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
y>-2,\,y<x.
$$

 

Combining this into a single condition, we have

$$
-2<y<x
$$

Since the boundary is not included in the set (the lines are dashed), the inequalities are strict.

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2<y<x}.
$$

Describe the shaded region shown above using set-builder notation.

$$
{(x,y)\in {{field-1}}\,:\,-2\,{{field-2}}\,y\,{{field-3}}\,2}
$$
after.worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *above* the line $y=-2$ and *below* the line $y=2.$

A point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
y>-2,\,y<2.
$$

Combining this into a single condition, we have

$$
-2<y<2.
$$

We must also include the line $y=2$ since the boundary is included in the set (the curve is solid). So, we change the corresponding inequality symbol above as follows:

$$
-2<y\le 2
$$

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2<y\le 2}.
$$

after.worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *to the right* of the curve $x=-{y}^{2}.$

Therefore, a point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following condition is satisfied:

$$
x>-{y}^{2}
$$

We must also include the curve $x=-{y}^{2}$ since the boundary is included in the set (the curve is solid). So, we change the inequality symbol above as follows:

$$
x\ge -{y}^{2}
$$

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,x\ge -{y}^{2}}.
$$

after.worked_solution:
Since all points $P(x,y)$ in our set lie at integer values of $x$ and $y,$ we have $x\in Z,y\in Z,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in Z\times Z={Z}^{2}.
$$

The points in our set include all those that lie *to the left* the line $x=2.$ For those points, the following condition is satisfied:

$$
x<2
$$

Since the boundary is *not* included in the set (the curve is *not* solid),  no further action must be taken, so we have

$$
x<2.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as follows:

$$
{(x,y)\in {Z}^{2}\,:\,x<2}
$$
